newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso hit by more speculation.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso hit by more speculation.

text.p: The Philippine peso was hit by another round of speculation early on Wednesday on renewed fears of a devaluation following a newspaper report, traders said.
The Singapore Strait Times reported in its Wednesday edition that Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said the devaluation of the peso will be taken up at the Monetary Board meeting today.
Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson and Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista denied the report.
The peso opened unchanged at 26.40 pesos to the dollar as the Central Bank sold dollars heavily to calm the market, dealers said. Volume in the market had already reached $687.25 million.
The Central Bank may have sold about $200 milion to $300 million at 26.40 pesos, traders said.
"The 30 percent overnight borrowing rate of the Central Bank should hurt speculators," a dealer said, adding it was the offshore players which had been preying on the peso.
